blockMcqs.question: What best describes a class?
options: A blueprint defining attributes and methods
A copy of an existing object
blockMcqs.explanation: A class only defines shape and behavior; it holds no data until an object is made.

blockMcqs.question: When does an object actually exist in memory?
blockMcqs.explanation: A class is just a definition; an object is created in memory when instantiated at runtime.

blockMcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches attributes and methods?
blockMcqs.explanation: Attributes hold an object's data (state); methods define what it can do (behavior).

blockMcqs.question: Why can two objects of the same class differ?
options: Only one of them has a constructor
blockMcqs.explanation: Objects share the class's behavior but each carries its own independent state.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main job of a constructor?
options: Set up an object's initial state on creation
Convert a class into an object type
blockMcqs.explanation: The constructor runs once at creation to initialize the new object's attributes.

blockMcqs.question: In the pseudocode, why do myCar and yourCar differ after accelerate()?
options: Each object tracks its own independent speed
Static state was shared between them
The constructor was skipped for one
blockMcqs.explanation: Each instantiation creates a separate object, so their speed attributes change independently.

blockMcqs.question: What does `this` (or `self`) point to inside a method?
options: The object the method is currently running on
blockMcqs.explanation: this/self lets a method access the attributes of the specific object it was called on.

blockMcqs.question: How does a static member differ from an instance member?
options: Static is per-object, instance is shared
Static is shared by the class, instance belongs to one object
blockMcqs.explanation: Static members have one copy shared across the class; instance members belong to each object separately.

blockMcqs.question: What typically reclaims an unused object in Java or Python?
blockMcqs.explanation: Garbage-collected languages automatically free objects once nothing references them anymore.

blockMcqs.question: What's the risk of using a static field where instance data was meant?
options: No risk, they behave the same
Every object ends up silently sharing one value
Only the first object gets a value
blockMcqs.explanation: A static field has one copy per class, so all objects read and overwrite the same shared value by mistake.
